title: Yakitori
subtitle: grilled chicken skewers with tare sauce
excerpt: Yakitori is skewered chicken grilled over high heat and glazed repeatedly with a sweet soy tare sauce. This home method uses a griddle pan or hot grill. Makes about 16 skewers, serving 4.
sourceNotes: Yakitori has been grilled on Japanese charcoal in izakaya and street stalls for over a century. Every neighbourhood has its yakitori shop. The tare sauce is the heart of the dish and each cook guards their own recipe.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The tare sauce keeps in the fridge for up to 2 weeks. Thread skewers up to 4 hours ahead and refrigerate.

glossaryTerms.definition: A concentrated seasoning sauce used in Japanese cooking, especially ramen and yakitori. Yakitori tare is made from soy, mirin and sake reduced together.
A Japanese pub-style restaurant where food and drinks are served together. Yakitori is one of the most common izakaya dishes.

content.text: The key to yakitori is the
sauce, which you brush on in layers as the chicken cooks. Each coat caramelises before the next goes on, building deep flavour. At home, a hot griddle pan works very well. Serves 4.
If using wooden skewers, soak them in water for 30 minutes first so they do not scorch on the heat.

items.prepNote: boneless, skin on, cut into 3cm pieces

content.text: Make the tare: combine soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer and cook for 5 minutes until slightly thickened. Pour into a small bowl and set aside.
Thread the chicken and spring onion pieces alternately onto skewers, pressing them close together.
Heat a griddle pan over high heat until very hot. Lay the skewers in the pan and cook for 2 minutes without moving.

Turn the skewers. Brush with tare sauce. Cook for 2 more minutes, then brush again with tare. Repeat this turning and brushing process twice more until the chicken is cooked through and well glazed, about 8 minutes total.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds if using. Serve immediately with cold beer or rice.

attrs.symptom: Tare sauce burns on the pan
attrs.cause: The sauce was applied too early or the heat was too high
attrs.fix: Only apply tare after the first turn. High sugar content burns quickly, so watch closely and reduce heat slightly.

attrs.cause: The griddle was not hot enough before the skewers went on
attrs.fix: Heat the griddle until smoking before adding skewers. Do not move them for the first 2 minutes.

attrs.symptom: Skewers taste bland without much glaze
attrs.fix: Build up layers. Turn and brush at least 3 times. Each coat needs 2 minutes to caramelise before the next.

content.text: culture, eaten with cold beer after work. Street stalls called yakitori-ya grill skewers over binchotan charcoal. No part of the chicken goes to waste in a proper yakitori shop: liver, heart, skin and cartilage all appear on the menu. Home cooks do not need charcoal to get good results. A very hot griddle and good tare get you most of the way there.
